name: Half-Angle Slicing for Incremental Lighting
aliases: Half-Angle Slicing for Incremental Lighting — Two-Pass Volumetric Shadow Setup
definition: A technique to compute volumetric shadows efficiently by using a pixel buffer to accumulate light attenuation from the light's point of view, avoiding the artifacts of volumetric shadow maps.
summary: Half-Angle Slicing for Incremental Lighting is a multipass technique that computes volumetric shadows using a 2D light buffer to decouple sampling from volume resolution, avoiding the memory overhead of 3D shadow maps.
